primary_sources_read.location: Chapter 6, Theorem 6.2, PDF page 91, source lines 3991-4009
primary_sources_read.comparison: The stated theorem applies to an integral monic cubic including its x-squared term. A finite-order rational point has y=0 or y squared dividing the polynomial discriminant. This verifies the exact theorem form used; no short-Weierstrass substitution is needed.

primary_sources_read.title: Explicit transformation of an intersection of two quadrics to an elliptic curve in Weierstrass form
primary_sources_read.read_scope: Primary paper abstract and bibliographic record, not a full proof comparison
primary_sources_read.comparison: Classical neighboring method: a rational-point-bearing smooth intersection of two quadrics has an explicitly constructed elliptic-curve isomorphism; applications include concordant forms and four rational squares in arithmetic progression. This does not establish the P11 ordered reconstruction or sixteen-root primitive theorem.
